prompt: A sign-up form checks whether a username is already taken.
tells: whether a username is already taken
why: The only question is yes or no: is this name already in the collection? Fast membership checks are what a hash set is for.
trap: Nothing is looked up but yes or no.

prompt: A web crawler skips pages it has already visited.
tells: skips pages it has already visited
why: Before crawling a page, the crawler asks whether it has seen it already. That yes-or-no check is a hash set.
trap: The queue holds pages to visit; 'already visited?' is a set.

prompt: Remove duplicate emails from a mailing list.
why: A set can hold each value only once, so adding every email to a set drops the repeats automatically.
trap: No value per email is needed.

prompt: A party door list only needs to answer one thing: is this guest invited?
why: There's nothing to look up about a guest, only whether they're on the list. A pure is-it-there check is a hash set.
trap: There's no extra value to fetch.

prompt: Count how many different countries visitors came from.
why: A set keeps one copy of each value, so put every country in a set and its size is the number of different countries.
trap: You need distinct values, not a count per country.

prompt: Find which songs appear in both of two playlists.
why: Put one playlist in a set, then check each song of the other against it in one step each. Checking membership is a set's job.
trap: No song needs a value attached.
